key_insight: How EEG seizure-prediction models were evaluated changed their scores far more than which of five architectures was used.
clinical_relevance: High retrospective scores may not translate to reliable seizure prediction for new patients or future seizures.
method: Kept five published pipelines fixed, from PSD+LDA to a transformer, on CHB-MIT EEG data.
Compared subject-held-out testing with random-window and chronological, intact-preictal-block splits within patients.
Traced windows for train–test overlap and tested the baseline without adaptation on Siena data.
evidence_signal: Across 20 subject-held-out partitions, mean AUCs were 0.527–0.553; within-patient PSD+LDA fell from 0.815 with random windows to 0.572 with chronological, intact-block testing.
watch_item: These results concern retrospective window classification, not continuous seizure alarms or demonstrated clinical utility.
paper_title: Same pipelines, different answers: how evaluation design shapes EEG seizure prediction
